name: Docker & Kubernetes
description: Containers from the Linux primitives up: Docker images and Compose, then Kubernetes workloads, networking and operations.

nodes.name: Containers vs VMs
nodes.desc: What containers are, how they differ from virtual machines and why they took over.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain what containers are, how they differ from virtual machines and why they became standard for shipping software.

nodes.name: Namespaces & cgroups
nodes.desc: The kernel features behind containers: namespaces, cgroups and union file systems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how Linux namespaces, cgroups and union file systems combine to create containers.

nodes.name: Docker basics
nodes.desc: Running, inspecting, stopping and removing containers with the Docker CLI.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run, inspect, stop and remove containers with the Docker CLI.
topics: Viewing logs and exec into containers

nodes.name: Dockerfiles
nodes.desc: Writing Dockerfiles, build context and instructions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write Dockerfiles that build reliable images using the right instructions and build context.

nodes.name: Images & registries
nodes.desc: Image layers, caching, tags, multi-stage builds and pushing to registries.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build small, cache-friendly images with multi-stage builds, tag them and push them to registries.

nodes.name: Volumes & networks
nodes.desc: Persistent data with volumes and container networking.
nodes.summary: You will be able to persist container data with volumes and connect containers through Docker networks.

nodes.name: Docker Compose
nodes.summary: You will be able to define and run multi-container applications with Docker Compose.

nodes.name: Compose app project
nodes.desc: Containerise a web app with a database and cache and run it with Compose.
nodes.summary: You will containerise a web app with a database and cache and run the whole stack with Docker Compose.

nodes.name: Kubernetes
nodes.desc: The control plane, nodes, the declarative model and kubectl.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe the Kubernetes control plane and nodes, its declarative model and use kubectl to manage resources.

nodes.name: Pods & Deployments
nodes.desc: Pods, ReplicaSets, Deployments, rolling updates and probes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to run workloads with Pods, ReplicaSets and Deployments, roll out updates and configure health probes.

nodes.name: Services & Ingress
nodes.desc: Service discovery, Service types and routing traffic in with Ingress.
nodes.summary: You will be able to expose workloads with Services and route external HTTP traffic in with Ingress.

nodes.name: ConfigMaps & Secrets
nodes.desc: Separating configuration and secrets from images.
nodes.summary: You will be able to keep configuration and secrets out of images using ConfigMaps and Secrets.

nodes.name: Persistent storage
nodes.summary: You will be able to give workloads persistent storage with PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses and StatefulSets.

nodes.name: Helm
nodes.desc: Packaging Kubernetes apps as Helm charts.
nodes.summary: You will be able to package and install Kubernetes applications as Helm charts with configurable values.

nodes.name: Autoscaling
nodes.desc: Resource requests and limits, horizontal pod and cluster autoscaling.
nodes.summary: You will be able to set resource requests and limits and scale workloads with horizontal pod and cluster autoscaling.

nodes.name: Observability
nodes.desc: Logs, metrics and debugging failing pods.
nodes.summary: You will be able to debug failing pods using logs, events, metrics and kubectl inspection.

nodes.name: Kubernetes security
nodes.desc: RBAC, network policies, pod security and image scanning.
nodes.summary: You will be able to secure a cluster with RBAC, network policies, pod security settings and image scanning.

nodes.name: Kubernetes app project
nodes.desc: Deploy a multi-service app to a cluster with a Helm chart, autoscaling and monitoring.
nodes.summary: You will deploy a multi-service app to a Kubernetes cluster with a Helm chart, autoscaling and monitoring.
